transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, I’m here because I keep forgetting things I’m supposed to do—scheduled callbacks, work orders, follow-ups I told people I’d handle. It’s gotten bad enough that everything’s piling up at work, and they sent me here before I mess up my chance to move up.
Besides forgetting things, have you noticed any other changes in your thinking, like confusion, trouble finding words, or getting lost in familiar places?
No, not really. I don’t think I’m getting confused or lost or anything like that. I can talk fine, as far as I know. It’s more that I realize I forgot to do something I was supposed to do.
Do you often forget tasks that you need to do in the future, like appointments or planned activities?

Yes. That’s basically the main problem. I forget scheduled callbacks, work orders, even simple follow-ups I told people I’d take care of. Then they pile up, and now work’s involved because they don’t want me losing my chance to move up.
Do you find it hard to remember to start tasks or take action on things you planned to do later, like calling someone back or starting an assignment?

Yes. That’s exactly what happens. I’ll mean to call someone back or start a work order later, and then it just doesn’t happen. Even basic follow-ups I told people I’d handle slip by me, and now it’s piled up enough that work sent me here before I lose my chance at moving up.
Do these memory issues happen even when you are not under the influence of any substances, medications, or after a head injury?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I haven’t noticed it being tied to anything like that. It just happens.
Have you noticed any other changes in your memory or thinking, such as difficulty recognizing familiar people, remembering recent events, or learning new information?
No, not really. I haven’t noticed anything like not recognizing people or not being able to remember recent things. It’s more just the stuff I’m supposed to do later that slips by me.
Do you have trouble remembering things you’ve just learned, like new names, phone numbers, or instructions?

Yeah, especially with instructions. Like if my supervisor is talking right to me about a repair or an audit, I’ll be looking at him and trying to listen, but only the first part really sticks. Then I end up having to ask him to repeat the rest.
Do you have trouble remembering things you knew well before, like familiar tasks, personal past events, or common knowledge?
No, I don’t think so. I can still do the familiar stuff and I remember my own past and general things. It’s not like I’m forgetting things I used to know well.
Do you often forget to do things at the time you intended, like remembering to call someone at a specific time or completing a task you planned to do later?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups I told people I’d handle later. It’s gotten so backed up that work sent me to get checked out before I miss my chance to move up.
Do you have trouble keeping track of multiple tasks or managing your time effectively, like prioritizing what to do first or organizing your workload?

I’m not really sure how to answer that one. I mean, I do have a lot going on at work sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about whether it’s time management or just the job being busy. I’d have to think about that more.
Do you often find it hard to get started on tasks or follow through with things you know you need to do, even if you remember them?

Yes. I’ll start a maintenance job and get the actual repair done, but then I leave the last parts hanging. Like I’ll forget to close the ticket, label the panel, or check back with the tenant. It’s not that I don’t know I’m supposed to do it—I just don’t follow it through all the way.
Do you find it hard to get started on tasks or activities on your own, even when you know you need to do them?

I’m not totally sure on that one. I know I have trouble finishing things off, but starting them on my own… I haven’t really paid attention to whether that’s a separate problem. I’d have to think about it.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities, like planning steps to complete a project or keeping track of what needs to be done?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it in terms of organizing the whole task or planning steps. I know there are times things don’t get wrapped up cleanly, but whether that’s because I’m not organizing it right… I don’t know.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?

I’m still not really sure. I know the stuff needs to get done, but I haven’t noticed clearly whether the hard part is starting it without someone reminding me. I can think more about it, but I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?

I honestly still don’t know how to answer that clearly. I know there are things I put off or don’t get done, but I haven’t paid enough attention to whether it’s because I can’t get started without a reminder. I’d probably have to watch for that more.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?

I’m sorry, I still don’t really have a clear answer for that. I know things sometimes sit there longer than they should, but I can’t say for sure if it’s because I can’t start them on my own or if it’s something else.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?

I don’t think I can give you a solid yes or no. I know I delay things sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed whether it’s specifically because I can’t start without a reminder. I don’t want to guess and give you the wrong answer.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?
I really don’t know. I’m trying to think of examples, but I can’t tell if it’s a “getting started” problem or just normal putting things off. I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Do you find it hard to start tasks on your own, even when you know you need to do them, like beginning a repair job or calling someone back without being reminded?

I’m still not sure how to answer that. I don’t really track whether I start things on my own or only after someone reminds me. I know stuff gets delayed sometimes, but I can’t honestly say it’s because of that specifically.
